call_points.text: Aadhaar project: ₹75 Cr invested of about ₹125 Cr; full investment done next quarter, full revenue from Q4.
Digital business won a West Bengal Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY mandate, a Tamil Nadu Grama Bank mandate and a Coverfox partnership.
Capital allocation priority is organic expansion, then M&A, then dividends; M&A investments are generating 17-20% returns.
On buybacks, management said it is not under consideration now but may be discussed at the next Board meeting.
Asked to quantify value created by acquisitions, management deferred the question to the CFO and moved on.
Management targets 20-25% revenue growth for FY27 on an increased base.
Visa and consular services saw strong traction with FY26 EBITDA growing 30% and margins expanding to 40%.
Digital services revenue more than doubled to ₹1,158 crores, registering a 114% YoY growth.
Phase 1 of the UIDAI Aadhaar project has been rolled out, with full implementation expected over the next 1 to 1.5 years.
Geopolitical tensions in West Asia have caused minor short-term impacts, but overall business growth remains steady across 80+ countries.
Net revenue per application in the visa business increased 14% to ₹3,302.

timeline.summary: BLS International completed the strike-off of its wholly owned subsidiary Reired BLS International Services on May 11, 2026.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹814.56 Cr (+17.6% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹177.8 Cr (+31.6% YoY).
BLS International reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹2,998.2 Cr and PAT of ₹723.8 Cr.
BLS International submitted the audio recording of its Q4 FY26 earnings call on May 20, 2026.
BLS International reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹2,998 Cr and PAT of ₹724 Cr, driven by growth in visa and digital services.

On 11 August 2026 BLS International's Q1FY27 call reported record quarterly revenue of ₹891 Cr (up 25%), EBITDA of ₹252 Cr and PAT of ₹202 Cr, with net cash of ₹1,617 Cr and reiterated 15-20% organic growth guidance.

watchlist.text: Shareholder approval for final dividend at the ensuing Annual General Meeting

watchlist.response: Management said M&A investments generate 17-20% returns and deferred the value-creation question to the CFO, who was not available.
watchlist.text: Analysts asked repeatedly for the economic value and returns created by past acquisitions (iDATA, Aadifidelis).

watchlist.response: CFO said buyback is not under consideration now but may be discussed at the next Board meeting; acquisitions remain the priority.
watchlist.text: Analysts pressed on why no buyback is being considered given ₹1,617 Cr net cash and ₹2,500 Cr reserves.

watchlist.response: CFO declined to comment without checking the numbers and asked the analyst to send details.
watchlist.text: An analyst said Visa gross profit ratio declined sequentially and asked why.

watchlist.response: CFO did not quantify it, saying some contracts conclude while new ones are won and 10-15% growth can be maintained.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked how much visa revenue will fall off from contracts expiring in the next 12 months.
